prerequisites: This subject has no prerequisites. However, it should be taken after successfully completing the first-year course 'Graphic Expression and Computer-Aided Design'.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and abilities to apply graphic engineering techniques.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.

Permanent self-learning. Use learning continuously and develop autonomous and flexible learning strategies throughout life to be part of an active, motivated, and integrated citizenry, favoring job improvement or personal development.

Knows and understands the fundamentals of industrial drawing to apply them to the creation and interpretation of drawings, both assembly and exploded, and to elaborate reasoned solutions to geometric problems in the plane and in space.
Values standardization as an ideal convention to simplify not only production but also communication, giving it a universal character.
Is able to integrate and select standardized and commercial elements in the design of mechanical assemblies, interpreting handbooks and catalogs.
Knows and understands various concepts such as tolerances and surface qualities and is able to apply them to specific problems in the field of Industrial Drawing.

syllabus_topics: Bearings, rolling bearings, and their accessories.
assessment_rules: The final grade is a weighted sum of a theoretical-practical exam (50%) and a practical work/project (50%). The theoretical-practical exam comprises a practical part (70% of the exam grade) and a theoretical part (30% of the exam grade). To pass, a minimum grade of 5.0 is required in both the practical work/project and the exam. If one part is failed, its grade is retained for the next call within the same academic year. Students may opt for a global evaluation test, which includes an additional mechanical assembly task with CAD software alongside the theoretical-practical exam.
